newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon to hang three Sunni Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon to hang three Sunni Islamists.

text.p: Lebanese authorities will execute three members of a radical Moslem group on Monday, more than two months after they were sentenced to death for killing a rival Islamist cleric in 1995, judicial sources said on Sunday.
They said Munir Abboud, a Palestinian, and Khaled Hamed and Ahmad al-Kasm, both Lebanese, will be hanged to death before dawn at Roumyeh jail north of Beirut.
The three members of Esbat al-Ansar faction, along with their leader Palestinian Ahmed Saadi who is at large, were sentenced to death on January 17 for the killing of Sheikh Nizar al-Halabi.

Halabi, who headed the pro-Syrian Sunni group al-Ahbash, was gunned down in his car in mainly-Moslem West Beirut in August 1995. Saadi was convicted of ordering his killing and the three others of carrying it out.
The sources said President Elias Hrawi signed on Friday the death sentences issued by Lebanon's highest court, the Judicial Council, paving the way for the executions.

Sunni Islamist clerics based in the southern port of Sidon had appealed to Hrawi to commute the sentences against the three, London-based Arabic newspapers said on Sunday. The group is based in Ain el-Hiwleh Palestinian refugee camp near Sidon.

"We will not hide the fact that we will take a religious and popular position that pleases our consciences and God if these young men are executed," the Meeting of Moslem Clerics said in a statement published by the newspapers.
Security sources said the Lebanese army tightened security in Sidon on Sunday to head off any possbile protests against the executions.
The court opened the trial of 20 group members, including Saadi and the three others, in May 1996 on charges of killing Halabi and belonging to a violent armed group.

The court had also sentenced two group members, a Palestinian and a Lebanese, to life in jail for their part in killing Halabi and two others received a 20-year and five-year jail terms respectively for previous attempts against his life.
Twelve men accused of belonging to Esbat al-Ansar (Band of Supporters) received shorter jail terms for carrying unlicenced weapons.
